hints.title: Unifying Championship Winners
hints.text: Unify winners from Wimbledon, French Open, US Open, and Australian Open into a single stream of winner player IDs.

hints.title: Counting Titles per Player
hints.text: Group the combined winner IDs by player ID and count occurrences to determine total grand slams.

hints.title: Joining Player Details
hints.text: Join the aggregated title counts with the Players table to retrieve player names.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    p.player_id,
    p.player_name,
    SUM(p.player_id = c.Wimbledon) +
    SUM(p.player_id = c.Fr_open) +
    SUM(p.player_id = c.US_open) +
    SUM(p.player_id = c.Au_open) AS grand_slams_count
FROM Players p
JOIN Championships c ON p.player_id IN (c.Wimbledon, c.Fr_open, c.US_open, c.Au_open)
GROUP BY p.player_id, p.player_name;
```

complexity.time: O(P * C) or O(C) with UNION ALL unpivot
complexity.notes: Unpivot of multiple competition columns with grouped count.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Four separate queries merged in application memory require multiple round trips.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Filtering on join condition with IN limits records to active title winners.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should demonstrate unpivot techniques or multi-column equality counting.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def grand_slam_titles(players: pd.DataFrame, championships: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    winners = pd.concat([championships["Wimbledon"], championships["Fr_open"], championships["US_open"], championships["Au_open"]])
    counts = winners.value_counts().reset_index()
    counts.columns = ["player_id", "grand_slams_count"]
    res = players.merge(counts, on="player_id")
    return res[["player_id", "player_name", "grand_slams_count"]]
solutions.approach: Series concatenation and value counts in pandas
